beats.headline: Shares rally 7.25% on reported CPU price increases
beats.explanation: AMD rose 7.25% to $220.27 on heavy volume that was 2.4 times its 30-day average. The advance was driven by reports that AMD and peer chipmakers plan double-digit price increases of roughly 15% for CPUs to address supply shortages and robust data center demand. This move was shared with competitor INTC, which also gained 7.08% on the same reports.

beats.headline: Stock jumps 7.80% to record high on AI momentum
beats.explanation: AMD gained 7.80% to close at $278.26, marking its 12th consecutive daily gain and setting a new record high on trading volume 3.15 times its average. The rally reflected expanding investor optimism regarding AI accelerator contracts and data center revenue growth. The gain was shared with competitor INTC, which rose 5.48%, whereas supplier TSM declined 3.13%.

beats.headline: Shares gain 6.67% amid broader AI chip demand rally
beats.explanation: AMD climbed 6.67% to $303.46 on trading volume 2.39 times normal levels. The rise was supported by a Wall Street price target increase from Stifel and broad-based demand for AI hardware. The move was shared across peers, with competitor AVGO advancing 5.09% and supplier TSM rising 5.26%.

beats.headline: Stock surges 13.91% after upgrade tied to Intel results
beats.explanation: AMD advanced 13.91% to $347.81 on 3.97 times average trading volume. The surge followed an upgrade by D.A. Davidson to Buy with a $375 price target, spurred by strong earnings from competitor INTC that signaled accelerated CPU demand from agentic AI workloads. This sharp rise was shared with INTC, which surged 23.60%, and competitor QCOM, which gained 11.12%.

beats.headline: Shares drop 3.79% following ARK share sale
beats.explanation: AMD declined 3.79% to $334.63 on trading volume 2.46 times its 30-day average. The pullback followed reports that Cathie Wood's ARK sold substantial shares after the stock's steep multi-week run. The drop was company-specific, as competitor NVDA rose 4.00% and competitor INTC gained 2.97% on the same day.

beats.headline: Stock leaps 18.61% on Q1 earnings beat and guidance
beats.explanation: AMD surged 18.61% to $421.39 on trading volume 4.27 times normal levels after filing its quarterly financial report. First-quarter results topped expectations, highlighted by a 57% jump in data center revenue and stronger-than-expected guidance for the second quarter. While competitor NVDA gained 5.77% and supplier TSM added 6.36%, AMD significantly outperformed the sector.

beats.headline: Shares jump 11.44% on Rackspace deal and CPU demand
beats.explanation: AMD gained 11.44% to close at $455.19 with volume reaching 2.83 times its average. The rally was driven by an AI cloud agreement with Rackspace and rising analyst optimism around agentic AI server CPU demand. The advance was shared across the sector, with competitor INTC rising 13.96% and competitor QCOM gaining 8.17%.

beats.headline: Stock rises 7.78% past $500 on OneQode AI deployment
beats.explanation: AMD rose 7.78% to finish at $503.89 on volume 1.87 times its 30-day average. The move followed an agreement with OneQode to deploy AMD Instinct GPUs and Helios rack-scale systems, alongside news that next-generation AI processors entered production. While competitor QCOM rose 4.48%, competitor NVDA declined 0.22% and customer MSFT fell 0.61%.

beats.headline: Shares fall 8.15% amid chip selloff despite power deal
beats.explanation: AMD dropped 8.15% to $454.62 on volume 1.77 times the average. The decline occurred despite AMD announcing a long-term AI infrastructure partnership with Core Scientific for up to 2.5 gigawatts of capacity, as broader concerns over AI infrastructure spending pressured the chip sector. The move was shared with competitors INTC, which fell 5.86%, and QCOM, which dropped 4.21%.

beats.headline: Stock surges 13.00% on Core Scientific deal and upgrade
beats.explanation: AMD climbed 13.00% to $485.39 on 1.80 times average volume. The rebound was propelled by a price target increase from Susquehanna and renewed market appreciation for the 2.5-gigawatt Core Scientific AI data center contract. The rally was shared with customer MSFT, which jumped 15.51%, and competitor INTC, which gained 11.30%.

beats.headline: Shares drop 7.04% post-Q2 earnings on high expectations
beats.explanation: AMD declined 7.04% to $482.05 on volume 2.41 times average following its second-quarter earnings release. Although AMD posted record quarterly revenue of $11.5 billion, the report failed to satisfy heightened market expectations, and sentiment was dampened by comments that SpaceX would use rival chips. The decline was largely company-specific, as competitor NVDA gained 3.44% and competitor INTC rose 0.20%.

beats.headline: AMD rises 9.95% to top $1T market cap on AI agent surge
beats.explanation: AMD gained 9.95% to close at $615.52 on 2.16 times average trading volume, pushing its market capitalization past $1 trillion for the first time. The rally was initiated by market excitement over Meta's Muse AI agent, which spurred expectations for surging CPU server demand. The move was shared across peers, with competitor INTC climbing 12.14% and competitor QCOM rising 9.29%.

arc: Between March and September 2026, AMD engineered a sustained ascent from $205.37 to $615.52, culminating in its entry into the $1 trillion market capitalization club. The central driver across the period was a structural surge in data center CPU and accelerator demand tied to agentic AI workloads, which enabled double-digit CPU price increases and drove a 57% surge in Q1 data center revenue alongside a record $11.5 billion top line in Q2. Significant multi-gigawatt infrastructure and hardware deployments—such as agreements with Rackspace, OneQode, and Core Scientific—solidified commercial adoption of AMD's Instinct GPUs and Helios platforms. Although the stock encountered intermittent setbacks from elevated earnings expectations and institutional profit-taking, the broader trajectory was defined by repeated upward price target revisions and industry-wide demand surges that AMD shared with key peers like Intel.
